records.summary: In an operator-run, read-only API-2 experiment on October 24, 2026, the July 25, 2026 live daily asset was successfully obtained using an explicitly selected one-hop Orbit-to-S3 redirect and compared with the complete, non-overlapping REST traversal for that test

records.summary: In a read-only API-2 experiment on October 24, 2026, a fresh, live August 7, 2026 daily asset and REST watering-event history both contained 21 identifiable nested irrigation events; the comparator matched all 21 without recognized-field differences
records.limits: Cause of the difference between observations is unknown, and no general retention, consistency, or completeness guarantee is inferred. The user provided report excerpts, not original private records

records.summary: The October 24, 2026 API-2 historical REST/asset comparison performed a bounded watering-history traversal. With requested per-page=14, the selected traversal observed 67 top-level history containers, zero duplicate-container observations and an EMPTY_PAGE termination, reported as pagination_exhausted=true.
records.limits: Applies only to the selected current collection, account and date. Exhausting this traversal does not establish complete archived watering history or a vendor retention limit.

records.summary: The October 24, 2026 API-2 direct-HTTP matrix compared selected watering-history pagination sizes. Requested per-page values 10, 14, 28, 50 and 100 yielded first/second-page counts 10/10, 14/14, 28/28, 50/17 and 67/0 respectively (HTTP 200). The run used 32 physical requests. Full 10- and 14-item traversals each found 67 containers and 831 nested irrigation records, no observed duplicate containers, and empty-page termination.
records.limits: Direct HTTP paging behaviour differed from an earlier browser report. These are bounded observations of one collection, not a stable pagination specification or proof of a fixed history-retention period.

records.summary: The October 24, 2026 authenticated API-2 matrix tested specific login fields and header omissions. The selected session response contained orbit_api_key and user/account identifier fields but no orbit_session_token. An API-key GET /v1/devices returned HTTP 200. Omitting Orbit-App-Id yielded HTTP 401; omitting Origin, Referer or User-Agent individually yielded HTTP 200 in the tested profile.
records.limits: Field presence and HTTP statuses apply to one session, account and endpoint. No universal credential/header contract, session-token non-support or downstream forwarding rule was established.

records.summary: A read-only API-2 endpoints experiment on October 25, 2026 inspected five fixed first-party REST routes. GET /v1/devices returned HTTP 200 with one device; GET /v1/zone_reports/{device_id} returned HTTP 302 without following the redirect; GET /v1/event_logs/{device_id} returned HTTP 200 with 100 elements; GET /v1/bhyve_accounts/{account_id} returned HTTP 200 with an object containing recognized top-level keys created_at, id and name; GET /v1/bhyve_accounts/{account_id}/devices returned HTTP 404. The selected run used 11 physical requests.
records.limits: The 100-item event-log array is not proven to be the full history; the 404 is account/profile-specific. No redirected zone-report body was read. Response keys were from a limited recognition set, not complete universal schemas.

records.summary: The October 26, 2026 API-4B/C read-only GET matrix evaluated selected routes from client-source research. Of 14 attempted GETs, ten returned HTTP 200, one zone-report GET returned HTTP 302 and three returned HTTP 404 (landscapes, weather forecast and nested account-devices). Four additional candidate routes were NOT_TESTED because suitable owner-bound identifier values were not available.
records.limits: A counted probe is not necessarily a physical-request total, and the 404 results do not establish universal endpoint absence. Unprobed ID-dependent routes must not be reclassified as 404.

records.summary: The October 26, 2026 API-4C experiment tested event-log pagination separately from watering-history pagination. An unparameterized event-logs GET returned an HTTP 200 array of 100. Explicit page=1&per-page=10 returned HTTP 200 with 100 entries; page=2&per-page=10 returned HTTP 200 with an empty array. The selected page-one and page-two payloads were unequal.
records.limits: These results do not establish a 100-item total, universal cap, reliable pagination or global ignoring of per-page. The watering-history route has different observed paging behaviour.

records.summary: The October 26, 2026 API-4B zone-report GET was classified without following the server redirect. GET /v1/zone_reports/{device_id} returned HTTP 302. The Location was HTTPS to a recognized Orbit-associated S3 host family, with an OTHER_PATH not matching the existing validated daily-asset allowlist; the target was NOT_FOLLOWED_UNVERIFIED_DESTINATION.
records.limits: Host-family recognition does not authenticate or authorize an arbitrary signed object path. The target resource, payload, exact URL, signed query and content type were not verified.

records.summary: The October 26, 2026 API-4C experiment tested three candidate routes previously known principally from public client source. GET /v1/devices/{device_id} returned HTTP 200 with a JSON object; GET /v1/landscape_descriptions/{device_id} returned HTTP 200 with an eight-element array; GET /v1/sprinkler_timer_programs returned HTTP 200 with a five-element array. Recognized device fields included id, name, status, num_stations and zones; recognized landscape/program rows included id, device_id and created_at.
records.limits: Allowlisted field names and array counts do not determine all keys, field types, requiredness, nested structure or cross-account behaviour.

records.summary: A corrected API-4B zone-redirect classifier completed a selected October 27, 2026 observation. One login and one zone-report GET used two physical requests. The GET returned HTTP 302 with a structurally categorized HTTPS Orbit-associated S3 destination, four to seven path segments, a selected-device segment and AWS-v4 query-field presence. Existing daily-asset allowlist match=false; authorized_to_follow=false; follow-up target requests=0.
records.limits: The target path, signed values and response body were not retrieved. The earlier classifier error was a local implementation defect. These observations are not authority to broaden destination rules.

records.summary: An October 27, 2026 API-4A comparison of July 25 watering history preceded the timestamp-label parser correction. The bounded run used 12 requests, observed 67 history containers and a successfully acquired one-event daily asset, but rest_structure_valid=false. The comparison was INCONCLUSIVE; its reported zero in-scope REST count resulted from rejecting the invalidly parsed collection.
records.limits: A failed structural parser is not proof of zero historical events. Neither agreement nor disagreement could be established in that run; an earlier API-2 comparison result was not thereby invalidated.

records.summary: A follow-up October 27, 2026 audit narrowed the reason the prior July 25 comparison failed. Across 67 returned history containers, the strict parser classified noncanonical_or_invalid_date=67 and timestamp_like_date=67 while accepting zero containers. Counts for malformed/missing/null irrigation categories were zero. REST traversal still ended with EMPTY_PAGE and rest_structure_valid=false.
records.limits: The aggregates suggest full timestamp-like labels rather than expected date-only strings but do not prove exact syntax/time zones. The parser failure cannot be interpreted as absence of watering.

records.summary: A corrected timestamp-aware API-4A audit on October 27, 2026 revisited July 25 watering events. All 67 history containers were structurally accepted; their date labels were full timestamps with offsets. With 12 physical requests and EMPTY_PAGE completion, the selected date had one REST event and one asset event, one provisional identity match, zero source-only entries, no recognized-field conflicts and an AGREEMENT classification.
records.limits: One-date, selected-field agreement does not prove general REST/archive equivalence, complete retention or universal event-identity semantics.

records.summary: An October 27, 2026 timestamp-aware API-4A audit compared August 7 REST and daily-asset watering events. The bounded run used 12 requests, reported valid REST structure and EMPTY_PAGE traversal, then found 21 REST events and 21 asset events. All 21 provisional identities matched, with no REST-only/asset-only events, recognized-field conflicts or date-boundary uncertainty; the selected date was classified AGREEMENT.
records.limits: The comparison proves only the selected-date observed fields. An earlier report of watering_events:null for that date remains an unresolved versioning/source discrepancy.

records.summary: The owner separately authorized one API-5B/B3 first-party zone-report no-follow experiment. The operator reported one login and one fixed zone-report GET (two physical HTTP requests). The GET returned HTTP 302; execution state FIRST_PARTY_302_CLASSIFIED, and DENY_NOT_AUTHORIZED prevented the signed-target request. The target used an Orbit-associated S3 variant with an unpinned path and unrecognized query-key profile.
records.limits: Neither the object body nor its origin/authenticity was verified. The one-run authorization was consumed, and no broader allowlist or production access was approved.

records.summary: API-5C/C1 conducted a single authorized selected-device comparison of event-log pages and sprinkler programs. Six GETs plus one session POST used seven physical HTTP requests. Event-log page 1 with per-page=10 and =50 returned the same 100-element JSON array; page 2 for both sizes returned identical empty arrays. Programs with and without a device_id filter returned the same canonicalized five-element JSON array.
records.limits: Event-log retention/cap and server paging rules remain unknown. Identical program arrays do not show whether the device_id filter was ignored or every program belonged to that device. No redirect target was followed or controller state modified.

records.summary: API-5C/C2 tested fixed API-key REST header variants for a single session and device-list endpoint. One session POST and five GET requests used six physical requests. GET /v1/devices baseline, OMIT_ORIGIN, OMIT_REFERER and OMIT_USER_AGENT each returned HTTP 200 with identical one-device canonical JSON arrays. Omitting Orbit-App-Id returned HTTP 401. A session-token-only case was skipped because the login did not issue that field.
records.limits: The apparent User-Agent omission may not remove a lower-level library default. These results do not establish global required headers, session-token invalidity or WebSocket authentication semantics.

records.summary: API-5C/C3 compared selected August 6–8, 2026 watering histories under a validated daily-asset-only follow policy. The run reported 16 physical requests, 68 REST history containers and 21 REST events in the selected window. August 7 had 21 REST events and 21 asset events matching on selected identity/field checks (AGREEMENT). August 6 and 8 had zero REST events but retrieved daily assets whose watering_events fields were explicit null, so both comparisons were INCONCLUSIVE.
records.limits: A retrieved daily asset with watering_events:null is not a verified zero-event array. The three-day comparison does not establish general completeness; the unresolved zone-report S3 target was not requested.

records.summary: The owner provided activity/no-activity dates from their records to contextualize the August 6–8 comparison. They reported irrigation activity on August 4, 7, 9–13, 15, 17–20, 23–27 and 31, and no activity on August 6 or 8. The two no-activity reports were consistent with zero REST records plus daily-asset explicit null on those dates.
records.classification: OPERATOR-REPORTED EXTERNAL CALENDAR SUMMARY — NOT AN API REQUEST
records.limits: The records, their provenance, independence and exact per-day counts were not examined; activity reports are not API event totals. Null may mean inactivity on these dates but is not proven to mean zero events generally. No new Orbit request occurred.

records.summary: API-5C/C3G obtained a fixed eight-day selection of private archived daily assets and then checked those same saved files offline. Nineteen physical requests were reported; eight JSON documents and eight checksum sidecars (16 private files) were written. Six dates had populated irrigation arrays with counts 25, 21, 1, 8, 15 and 2 (72 total entries); two dates had explicit null. The subsequent checksum-verified local calendar reconciliation was day-level consistent for all eight selected dates.
records.classification: OPERATOR-REPORTED LIVE ASSET CAPTURE + OFFLINE SAME-FILE INTEGRITY CHECK
records.limits: The offline recheck is not independent vendor data; the separate owner calendar did not establish event counts. The two null entries remain structurally unknown, not zero arrays. Private archived files and identifiers are not published.

records.summary: API-5C/C4 evaluated unresolved REST routes against existing source-code candidates and earlier observations without new live calls. Seven routes were triaged: four were historically NOT_TESTED_ID_MISSING (mesh, topology, user, feedback); three had prior one-profile HTTP 404 results (landscapes, weather forecast, nested account-devices). This stage produced zero new route confirmations and no REST request.
records.classification: SOURCE-ONLY OFFLINE ROUTE AND IDENTIFIER RECONCILIATION
records.limits: Field presence is not permission to retrieve user information. Prior 404s are not proof of universal endpoint absence; a NOT_TESTED route is not a failed request. The decision matrix is offline analysis only.

records.summary: API-5C/C4-B scanned metadata fields in eight previously captured, checksum-verified local daily assets. The selected metadata positions contained mesh_id in 8/8 assets and user_id in 8/8, while topology_id, network_topology_id and bhyve_account_id were absent in those inspected positions. The scanner made zero network requests and did not output identifier values.
records.limits: Presence alone does not establish field location, cross-date equality, owner binding, endpoint existence or authorization. These are local historical clues rather than live Orbit response tests.

records.summary: API-5C/C4-C compared identifier locations and equality across eight local, checksum-verified assets. mesh_id and user_id were both present in the immediate nested device metadata of all eight assets, with equal values respectively across the eight snapshots and no conflicting sampled positions. No root-level device_id was present in these files. The scanner made zero network requests and exported no ID values or hashes.
records.classification: OPERATOR-REPORTED OFFLINE LOCAL METADATA CONSISTENCY OBSERVATION
records.limits: Correlated snapshots from one controller are not independent owner-identity proof. Missing root device_id does not imply nested device identity mismatch. A later offline step was required to compare nested device.id.

records.summary: API-5C/C4-D inspected nested device identifiers in the same eight saved archive pairs. Nested device.id matched the privately selected controller in 8/8 assets; alternative immediate device.device_id was missing in all eight. Stable mesh_id and user_id fields appeared within each matched nested device metadata object. No network requests, controller changes, raw IDs or hashes were exported.
records.limits: These are correlated local archive snapshots, not current server attestations, authenticated owner binding, mesh GET authorization or proof of a universal resource relationship.

records.summary: API-5C/C4-E performed one independently authorized first-party GET of an owner-selected historical mesh reference. One login and one mesh GET used two physical requests. GET /v1/meshes/{mesh_id} returned HTTP 200, application/json and a JSON object with top-level id, devices (array) and created_at keys. The request used a reference validated against eight local archived device snapshots.
records.limits: This experiment did not compare returned id with requested mesh_id or inspect device array members, length or selected-controller membership. It does not establish full response schema or universal endpoint availability.

records.summary: API-5E/E1 conducted six selected first-party GET observations for a single account/controller on November 2, 2026. One login and six GETs totalled seven physical requests: /v1/users/{user_id} returned 200 and matched the selected user ID; /v1/user_feedback?user_id= returned 200 with 11 object records; /v1/landscapes, /v1/weather_forecast/{device_id} and nested account-devices each returned 404; /v1/meshes/{mesh_id} returned 200, matching the selected mesh ID and exposing a one-object devices array.
records.limits: The user-feedback content was not exported. The mesh array record included a device_id key but its value was not compared to the selected controller. Three 404s are account/profile-specific; no complete schema or global support claim is warranted.

records.summary: API-5E/E2 inspected a single selected WebSocket connection after one owner-account login. The owner reported one WSS attempt, one app_connection using the REST API key under orbit_session_token, one JSON application ping and a single receive item classified INVALID_OR_OVERSIZED, followed by CONNECTION_CLOSED_OR_ERROR. No recognized server JSON application event was captured or controller command sent.
records.classification: OPERATOR-REPORTED BOUNDED LIVE WEBSOCKET TRANSPORT OBSERVATION
records.limits: The diagnostic combined several invalid-frame and closing causes; it did not establish an accepted application authentication, subscription, credential rejection, valid pong or server close code.

records.summary: API-5E/E2b performed a separate fixed-scope frame-level check on November 2, 2026. One frame was classified as CLOSE with EMPTY payload after a JSON application ping. No recognizable RFC 6455 close code was available. Login was reported successful; no valid application event or controller control message was observed.
records.classification: OPERATOR-REPORTED BOUNDED LIVE WEBSOCKET FRAME DIAGNOSTIC
records.limits: This was a distinct invocation from API-EV-072, not proof that the earlier invalid receive item was the same frame. Application authentication, device subscription, close reason and server event schema remain unverified. The frozen full model was not promoted based on this transport diagnostic.
